title: Decision of the AI Office
summary: This policy outlines the AI Office’s role in deciding on AI initiatives, detailing its responsibilities, and setting procedures for approvals and oversight. It also establishes guidelines for accountability and compliance to promote responsible AI use across the organization.

title: AI Office Vacancy: Technology Specialists in AI
summary: The policy outlines how the organization will recruit and hire technology specialists for its AI office. It specifies the qualifications, roles, and hiring procedures needed to build a skilled team that supports the company’s AI initiatives.

title: AI Office Vacancy: Lead Scientific Adviser
summary: The policy announces that the AI Office is seeking to fill the position of Lead Scientific Adviser. It outlines the role’s responsibilities, qualifications, and how the adviser will guide scientific research and strategy for AI initiatives.

title: AI Office Vacancy: Legal Officers
summary: The policy outlines the hiring process for legal officers in the organization’s AI office, detailing required qualifications, responsibilities, and application procedures. It emphasizes the importance of legal oversight, compliance, and ethical considerations in the development and deployment of AI systems.

title: AI Office Vacancy: Policy Officers
summary: The policy outlines how to fill vacant AI policy officer positions in the organization, detailing the qualifications needed for the role. It explains the application and selection process and the responsibilities that come with the position.

title: AI Act Scientific Panel
summary: The AI Act Scientific Panel is a group of experts that gives scientific and technical advice to help shape the EU’s AI regulations. They review AI technologies, assess risks, and recommend safety measures to make the law evidence‑based and effective.

title: Draft Standardisation Request
summary: The document is a draft request for establishing standardized guidelines and best practices for AI development, deployment, and oversight. It aims to harmonize policies across organizations, ensuring consistent safety, transparency, and accountability in AI systems.

title: CoP Consultation Notice
summary: The document announces a consultation process for a Community of Practice (CoP) framework. It invites stakeholders to review and provide feedback on the proposed guidelines and procedures.

title: CoP Call for Expression of Interest
summary: The CoP Call for Expression of Interest invites people and organisations to sign up and show their interest in joining a Community of Practice around AI policy. Participants will collaborate on discussions, share best practices, and help shape AI governance initiatives.

title: CoP Graphic: Overview of Iterative Drafting Process
summary: The document is a visual guide that outlines how the Community of Practice (CoP) drafts and revises its policies in a step‑by‑step, iterative manner. It shows each drafting phase, the feedback loops, and how stakeholders collaborate to refine and improve the policy over time.

title: CoP Graphic: Timeline of Drafting Process
summary: The document is a graphic that outlines the step-by-step drafting timeline for the CoP AI policy, showing when each phase of development takes place. It highlights key milestones such as initial drafting, stakeholder reviews, revisions, and final approval dates.

title: Code of Practice: 1st Draft
summary: This document is the first draft of a code of practice for AI systems, outlining the guidelines and principles that developers and users should follow. It aims to promote responsible, safe, and ethical AI use, covering areas such as transparency, accountability, fairness, and risk management.

title: Code of Practice: 2nd Draft
summary: The Code of Practice: 2nd Draft outlines a set of guidelines that govern the development, deployment, and use of AI systems, emphasizing safety, transparency, and accountability. It aims to provide clear standards for responsible AI practice, ensuring that stakeholders adhere to best practices while mitigating risks and promoting ethical outcomes.

title: Code of Practice: 3rd Draft
summary: This document is the third draft of a Code of Practice intended to provide clear guidelines for the responsible use of AI technologies. It outlines principles, procedures, and accountability measures to ensure that AI development and deployment comply with ethical, legal, and societal standards.

title: AI Pact Draft
summary: The AI Pact Draft is a proposed agreement that aims to create shared principles for responsible AI development and use, emphasizing transparency, fairness, safety, and accountability. It encourages collaboration among governments, industry, and civil society to establish guidelines and oversight mechanisms that ensure AI technologies benefit everyone ethically.

title: AI Pact Final
summary: The AI Pact Final is a comprehensive agreement that sets out standards, responsibilities, and best practices for developing and using artificial intelligence. It aims to promote safety, transparency, fairness, and accountability across AI systems worldwide.

title: Guidelines on prohibited artificial intelligence (AI) practices
summary: This policy outlines which AI activities are disallowed, such as using AI for manipulation, discrimination, or other harmful purposes. It aims to promote ethical and safe AI use by clearly defining prohibited behaviors.

title: Guidelines on AI System Definition
summary: This policy outlines how to identify and describe what counts as an AI system. It provides criteria and examples to help organizations determine if their technology qualifies as AI.

title: Communication on Boosting Start-Ups & Innovation
summary: This policy outlines strategies for encouraging start-ups and fostering innovation through targeted communication efforts. It emphasizes collaboration, resource sharing, and supportive messaging to accelerate entrepreneurship and technological advancement.

title: EuroHPC Initiative for Start-Ups
summary: The EuroHPC Initiative for Start‑Ups aims to help early‑stage companies access high‑performance computing resources and expertise. It provides funding, training, and collaborative opportunities so startups can develop and scale technology using EuroHPC’s advanced infrastructure.

title: Slideshow: Webinar on Risk Management
summary: This webinar will cover key concepts in risk management, including identifying potential risks, evaluating their impact, and developing strategies to mitigate them. Attendees will also learn how to implement risk assessment tools and maintain compliance with relevant regulations.

title: Video: Webinar on Risk Management
summary: The webinar titled “Video: Webinar on Risk Management” discusses core principles for identifying, assessing, and mitigating risks in AI projects. It offers practical guidance on establishing safeguards, monitoring risk throughout the AI lifecycle, and ensuring compliance with relevant regulations.
